scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02 on VLAN 10 answering DNS lookups from a domain member and replicating zone data between them.
scene.completeCaption: Both controllers answer for sbd.test and its reverse zone, with zone data replicated between them, and a member still finds a domain controller when either one is down. Proven, not assumed.

nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: Domain controller and DNS server built in course 1.1. In this course it hosts the AD-integrated zones and answers lookups for every domain member.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.title: SBD-DC02 · 10.0.10.11
nodes.description: The second domain controller and DNS server. It holds the same zones through directory replication and answers when SBD-DC01 can't.

nodes.name: TEST CLIENT
nodes.title: Test client · domain member viewpoint
nodes.description: Where lookups are run from: a domain member that lists both controllers for DNS. It stands for any member, not a system this course builds.

chapters.network: Both controllers run DNS on VLAN 10. The paths from the domain member to each controller are rule F01, TCP and UDP 53: a member has to find a controller before any Kerberos, LDAP, or Group Policy traffic can start.

The arc between the controllers is Active Directory replication carrying the sbd.test and 10.0.10.in-addr.arpa zone data, not a zone transfer. No member traffic is shown while the zones are configured.
Records created on one controller reach the other through directory replication. The animation represents that relationship, not a measured packet capture.

Follow lookups from the domain member to each controller, and to the remaining one during the failover test. Replication between the controllers stays in view because DCDiag and the replication summary check it.
Every path the course built is shown: lookups to both controllers and replication between them. Work through them one layer at a time when a name fails to resolve.
